newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gothaer and Berlin-Koelnisch join to form Parion.
newsitem.headline: Gothaer and Berlin-Koelnisch join to form Parion.

text.p: German insurers Gothaer Versicherungen and Berlin-Koelnischen Versicherungen on Monday said they had linked up to create a new firm called Parion.

Wolfgan Peiner, the new group's chairman, said last week's announcement by reinsurer Munich Re that it planned to acquire Victoria Holding AG showed that German insurers had to link up to improve their chances of survival.
"The smaller and medium-sized insurers have no competitive chance against large firms in the European market if they do not find their own solutions," Peiner said in a statement.
Both firms want to coordinate their company objectives and pool resources more effectively.

Parion said members of the separate component parts of the two firms had agreed to the founding of the joint company at a meeting last week. The operations have a combined consolidated premium income of more than five billion marks ($2.9 billion).

The Berlin-Koelnischen Lebensversicherung, Berlin-Koelnischen Krankenversicherung, Gothaer Lebensversicherung and Gothaer Versicherungsbank remain legally independent under the deal and the names Gothaer and Berlin-Koelnisch will continue to be used. ($ = 1.747 German Marks)
